newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ACPC export cuts won't cause price volatility - ICO.
newsitem.headline: ACPC export cuts won't cause price volatility - ICO.

text.p: A move by a group of top coffee producers to reduce exports will not cause price volatility, International Coffee Organization (ICO) executive director Celsius Lodder said on Monday.
"It will not add to volatility. They are just planning ahead ... to avoid volatility," Lodder said.
Lodder said the move was aimed at making prices for robusta stable.

He was referring to a plan by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to lower the exports of its 14 members by 1.3 million 60-kg bags to 24.98 million bags between January and June of this year.
The group had previously decided to limit members' exports to 26.28 million bags.

The ACPC decided at its meeting in Brazil on January 23 that arabica coffee producers would export 300,000 fewer bags and the remaining export cuts would come from countries producing the robusta variety.
Lodder said he expected coffee prices to be generally stable in 1997, with sporadic fluctuations. He added that he expected prices to average between 1.25 and 1.30 cents per lb.

The export cuts were initiated by African countries in a bid to lift robusta prices. Indonesian trade sources said Jakarta had proposed lowering its own exports by just 150,000 bags, leaving the rest of the cuts to African countries.
Ivory Coast Minister for Commodities Guy-Alain Gauze is expected to chair a meeting of robusta producers on Thursday to decide the size of other countries' export cuts.

He said stocks in importing countries were around six million to seven million bags. "Stocks are quite low at about six percent of demand compared with 10 to 14 percent last year. Certified and non-certified stocks are six to seven million bags," he said.
He said strategic stocks, which are used by countries to supply their domestic markets, are being kept near zero.
"The cost of keeping the stocks is very high, so they are reducing to minimum (levels). Roasters' strategic stocks allow them to supply their market for up to one month," he said.
